Timeline::add_days¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::add_days(int days) const

Move By Civil Days¶

add_days() changes the local calendar date while preserving the local clock fields. It is for rules stated as tomorrow at the same local time, three calendar days earlier, or the corresponding wall-clock appointment next day.

A civil day and 24 elapsed hours are not always the same interval. Timezone offset changes can make the instant-to-instant distance 23 or 25 hours even though the displayed date advances by exactly one. This distinction is why add_days(1) is intentionally different from add_hours(24) and from adding a fixed one-day Duration.

Daylight-Saving Transitions¶

The method reads each instant in the timeline’s timezone, moves its civil date, and resolves the same hour, minute, second, and nanosecond on that date. The destination’s UTC offset is then applied.

Example 1. Across the spring offset change, the local clock remains 03:30. The same source plus 24 elapsed hours lands at 04:30.

const auto spring = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-09T10:30:00Z")
                        .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    spring, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    spring.add_days(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    spring.add_hours(24), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-03-09T03:30:00.000000000-07:00"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-03-10T03:30:00.000000000-06:00"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-03-10T04:30:00.000000000-06:00"

Example 2. Inspecting epoch nanoseconds proves that the calendar-day result is 23 elapsed hours after the source in this transition.

std::cout << pluss::series::print(
    spring.add_days(1).epoch_nanos() - spring.epoch_nanos()) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[1], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=[82800000000000]

At the autumn transition the same rule can span 25 elapsed hours. The method’s guarantee is the local date and clock, not a constant epoch-nanosecond delta.

Signed Counts, Precision, And Mutation¶

days is signed: positive moves forward, negative moves backward, and zero preserves the instant. All subsecond digits are retained. The method is out-of-place and applies one scalar count to every logical element; it does not mutate the source or broadcast a second operand.

Example 3. Positive, negative, and zero counts preserve nanoseconds.

const auto precise = pluss::timeline::make(
    "2024-12-31T23:59:30.123456789Z");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    precise.add_days(1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    precise.add_days(-1), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    precise.add_days(0), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2025-01-01T23:59:30.123456789+00:00"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-12-30T23:59:30.123456789+00:00"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"2024-12-31T23:59:30.123456789+00:00"

Shape, Timezone, And Absence¶

Scalar, vector, matrix, and higher-rank timelines are accepted. The returned timeline has the same shape and timezone label. Logical strides are respected, NaT remains NaT, and zero-sized dimensions are preserved.

Example 4. An absent instant propagates while the defined value moves three civil days.

const auto values = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    {1'704'067'200'123'456'789LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT}, "UTC");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    values.add_days(3), "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["2024-01-04T00:00:00.123456789+00:00", "NaT"]

Example 5. Empty rank is metadata, not an error.

const auto empty = pluss::timeline::epoch({0, 2}).add_days(1);
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::timeline::format(
    empty, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[0, 2], dim=2, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Nonexistent And Ambiguous Local Clocks¶

If the preserved wall clock does not exist on the destination date, the method throws instead of silently moving the timestamp. A repeated clock at an autumn transition resolves to its first occurrence. Use fixed elapsed arithmetic when you want to cross transitions without requesting a particular local clock.

Example 6. 02:30 exists on March 9 but not on the spring-transition date in this timezone, so adding one civil day is rejected.

try {
  const auto before = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-09T09:30:00Z")
                          .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
  (void)before.add_days(1);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected
